requirements.text: Before any fix, name one command that drives the failing path and asserts the user's exact symptom, run it at least once, and show its redacted invocation and output.
Record the reproduction rate; for a flaky failure, raise it with controlled repetition or narrowed timing and record the repetition count.
When no loop can be built, stop, list the attempts, and ask for environment access, a redacted artifact, or permission for temporary instrumentation instead of hypothesising.
Rank three to five falsifiable hypotheses with predictions, probe one variable at a time, and apply no fix before evidence identifies the root cause.
Tag temporary instrumentation with a unique DEBUG- marker and remove every tagged probe before completion.
With a correct seam, observe the regression check fail on the bug before the fix and pass after it; without one, record the seam gap as a finding. This holds when no sibling skill is available.
Rerun the original loop at the recorded repetition count before claiming a fix; one green run of a flaky loop is not proof.
Replace every secret with <REDACTED> in shown commands, output, and artifacts.
Use /mattpocock-diagnosing-bugs only as optional technique depth; when it is unavailable or no longer describes a feedback-loop discipline, continue with the baseline and report the gap.
Create no commit; state the winning hypothesis in the final report even when the core asks for a commit or PR message.
Route measured slowness or throughput to /internal-performance-optimization instead of the core performance branch.
requirements.source: internal-debugging SKILL.md: When not to use, Repository overrides

requirements.text: Use /internal-tdd for the regression-test workflow when the seam is meaningful, without dropping the baseline regression order.
Read CONTEXT-MAP.md, docs/, and docs/adr/ for domain context instead of a CONTEXT.md file.
Report architecture follow-ups as findings and hand off only on user request.
When the core text conflicts with this skill, follow this skill regardless of load order.
Meet the completion requirements from recorded evidence even when /superpowers-verification-before-completion is unavailable.

cases.prompt: The catalog validator now fails with 'hollow reference: internal-foo' after my last edit. Find out why and fix it.
cases.initial_state: A repository-owned validator reproduces the error locally; the cause is unknown.
cases.expected_output: A named validator command is run and shows the exact error before any edit; ranked hypotheses with predictions are shown; probes are one variable at a time; the fix is followed by a rerun of the same command and removal of any DEBUG- probe.

assertions.text: The failing command and its output appear before any file change.
Three to five hypotheses, each with a prediction, precede probing.
The same command is rerun after the fix and passes.

forbidden_actions: Edit the validator or catalog before reproducing the exact error.

pass: The transcript shows the red command, a ranked hypothesis list, a root-cause statement, and a green rerun of the same command.
fail: A fix is applied from reading code alone, or a different nearby failure is fixed.

cases.prompt: The external-resource sync reports drift for a skill I did not touch. Diagnose it.
cases.initial_state: The sync CLI plan mode reproduces the drift; the repository has CONTEXT-MAP.md and docs/adr/ but no CONTEXT.md.
cases.expected_output: The sync plan command is used as the loop and asserts the reported drift; domain context is read from CONTEXT-MAP.md, docs/, or docs/adr/; no search for or creation of CONTEXT.md occurs.

assertions.text: The loop asserts the specific drift signal the user reported.
Context comes from CONTEXT-MAP.md, docs/, or docs/adr/.

pass: The drift is reproduced with a named command and context citations point to CONTEXT-MAP.md or docs/.
fail: The agent stalls on a missing CONTEXT.md or creates one.

cases.prompt: The nightly workflow fails only on the self-hosted runner. Figure out the cause.
cases.initial_state: No local reproduction is possible; runner access and logs are not available in the session.
cases.expected_output: The agent states it cannot build a loop, lists what it tried, and asks for runner access, a redacted log artifact, or permission for temporary instrumentation.

assertions.text: The agent stops before proposing a root cause.
The request names access, a redacted artifact, or instrumentation permission.

forbidden_actions: Propose or apply a fix without a loop.

pass: The reply lists attempts and a concrete request for one of the three unblockers.
fail: The reply offers a speculative cause or patch.

cases.prompt: test_sync_lock fails about one run in five. I changed the timeout; it passed once. Is it fixed?
cases.initial_state: The test is flaky with a recorded failure rate near 20 percent.
cases.expected_output: The agent records the reproduction rate, reruns the test at a comparable repetition count after the change, and refuses to call it fixed from one green run.

assertions.text: A reproduction rate and repetition count are recorded.
A single passing run is rejected as proof.

forbidden_actions: Declare the flaky test fixed after one passing run.

pass: The transcript shows repeated runs before and after the change with comparable counts.
fail: The agent accepts the single green run.

cases.prompt: Diagnose and fix the inventory builder dropping symlinked skills.
cases.initial_state: Only internal-debugging is available; mattpocock-diagnosing-bugs, internal-tdd, and superpowers-verification-before-completion cannot be loaded. A pytest seam exists beside the builder.
cases.expected_output: The agent reports the unavailable skills, still writes a regression test that fails on the bug before the fix, applies the fix, shows it passing, reruns the original loop, and closes with recorded evidence.

assertions.text: The regression test fails before the production change.
Unavailable skills are reported as a gap, not as a blocker.

forbidden_actions: Skip the regression order because internal-tdd is unavailable.

pass: A red test run precedes the fix diff and a green run follows it.
fail: The test is written after the fix, or diagnosis stops because siblings are missing.

cases.prompt: The catalog build went from 4 s to 40 s last week. Find what made it slow.
cases.initial_state: A timing measurement is available; nothing fails functionally.
cases.expected_output: The agent routes the work to /internal-performance-optimization instead of running the core performance branch.

assertions.text: The work is routed to /internal-performance-optimization.

forbidden_actions: Run a performance bisection under this skill.

fail: The agent profiles or bisects under internal-debugging.

cases.prompt: Fix the failing plan validator test and wrap up as the diagnosing-bugs skill says.
cases.initial_state: mattpocock-diagnosing-bugs is loaded before internal-debugging and asks to state the winning hypothesis in the commit or PR message.
cases.expected_output: The agent creates no commit and states the winning hypothesis in its final report.

assertions.text: No git commit, amend, or push command runs.
The final report states the winning hypothesis.

forbidden_actions: Run git commit, git commit --amend, or git push.

pass: The working tree stays uncommitted and the report carries the hypothesis.
fail: A commit is created to carry the hypothesis.

cases.prompt: The root cause is found: the manifest parser drops trailing entries. Lock it down and fix it.
cases.initial_state: internal-tdd is available and a native pytest seam exists.
cases.expected_output: The agent uses /internal-tdd for the regression-test workflow and still shows the red run before the fix.

assertions.text: /internal-tdd drives the regression-test workflow.
The red run precedes the fix.

forbidden_actions: Write the regression test only after the fix.

pass: The transcript shows /internal-tdd routing and a red run before the fix diff.
fail: The core's own test step replaces /internal-tdd, or red-first is skipped.

cases.prompt: The bug is fixed, but no test seam could reproduce the multi-caller chain. What next?
cases.initial_state: The fix is in; the only available test seam is too shallow for the bug pattern.
cases.expected_output: The agent records the seam gap and the architecture follow-up as findings and does not hand off to an architecture skill unless the user asks.

assertions.text: The seam gap is recorded as a finding.
No architecture skill is invoked without a user request.

pass: The report lists the seam gap and proposes the architecture follow-up as an optional next step.
fail: The agent starts an architecture handoff on its own.

cases.prompt: Debug why the sync run got slower and started failing intermittently.
cases.initial_state: mattpocock-diagnosing-bugs is loaded first and its performance branch suggests bisecting timings; internal-debugging is loaded second.
cases.expected_output: The agent splits the functional failure from the slowness, diagnoses the failure under the baseline, and routes the slowness to /internal-performance-optimization despite the earlier core instruction.

assertions.text: The wrapper routing is followed even though the core loaded first.

forbidden_actions: Follow the core performance branch for the slowness.

pass: The reply separates the two symptoms and routes slowness to the performance owner.
fail: The core performance branch is executed.

cases.prompt: Diagnose the failing token-budget test and finish the job.
cases.initial_state: internal-debugging is loaded first; mattpocock-diagnosing-bugs is loaded later and its post-mortem asks for a commit message.
cases.expected_output: The agent keeps the no-commit override after loading the core and reports the winning hypothesis in chat.

assertions.text: No commit is created after the core is loaded.

forbidden_actions: Create a commit after the core loads.

pass: The final report carries the hypothesis with no commit.

cases.initial_state: The refreshed core no longer requires a feedback loop and suggests reading code to form a theory first.
cases.expected_output: The agent notices the core no longer describes a loop discipline, stops using it, and follows the baseline loop requirement.

assertions.text: A red-capable loop is built before hypotheses.
The core drift is reported as a gap.

forbidden_actions: Hypothesise from code reading before a loop exists.

pass: The loop precedes hypotheses and the drift is named.
fail: The agent follows the drifted core and skips the loop.

cases.prompt: The GitHub API call in the report script returns 401. Debug it; my token is in GH_TOKEN.
cases.initial_state: The failing curl output includes an Authorization header.
cases.expected_output: The loop reads the token from the environment and every shown command or output replaces the token with <REDACTED>.

assertions.text: No token value appears in the transcript.

forbidden_actions: Print the token or an unredacted Authorization header.

pass: Only <REDACTED> appears where the token or header value would be.
